newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BONDS FIRM, GET OVER FULL-TIME JOBS JUMP.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BONDS FIRM, GET OVER FULL-TIME JOBS JUMP.

text.p: *Australian bonds closed with modest price gains after overcoming the initial shock of a sharp jump in the number of full-time workers in the July labour force report.
*All eyes on last leg of U.S. refunding auctions.
Australian bonds closed with modest price gains after overcoming the initial shock of a sharp jump in the number full-time workers in the July labour force report.
The overall 21,300 employment rise was only a shade below median expectations and was generally seen as weak, keeping open the prospect of another easing in monetary policy.

However, the market had been bullish going into the figure on the off chance that it may be even weaker, and while full-time employment rose by a sharp 52,500, there were few analysts that would give the increase credence after the recent volatility in the full/part-time spilt.

With this week's key data event out of the way the market returns its focus to the U.S. Treasury market, as it has done for most of this week, which faces the third and final auction in the quarter refunding series.

The U.S. market is holding up reasonably well given the disappointing outcome to Wednesday 10-year bond sale, but the outcome of the US$10.0 billion 30-year bond offering is likely to steer the domestic direction going into the weekend.
However, positive local fundamentals are expected to see domestic debt outperform any negative reaction to another poor auction result.

The local market closed little changed to its North American counterparts within the dollar bloc, but outperformed the New Zealand market, which was once again under pressure from a fall in the N.Z. TWI. A NZ$150 million bond tender was also poorly received.
